chapters.title: Market in 30 seconds
chapters.text: Good morning. This is Springpad Today, edition one forty four, for Thursday, the twelfth of November. Here is what happened in Wednesday's session, and what it means for you. Markets came back from the Diwali holiday in a good mood. The Sensex rose seven hundred and seventy three points, almost one per cent, to close at eighty one thousand, eight hundred and seventy nine. The Nifty gained two hundred and ten points, to end at twenty five thousand, two hundred and fifty five. Banks did the heavy lifting, and smaller companies did even better. The Nifty Smallcap index rose one point six per cent.

chapters.title: Foreign investors are back
chapters.text: Story one. Foreign investors are back, and in a big way. On Wednesday, they bought about twelve and a half thousand crore rupees more of Indian shares than they sold. Domestic funds did the opposite, and sold about eight thousand four hundred crore, booking profits. Foreign funds have also been cutting their bets against the Nifty. Their short positions in index futures fell from about two point four lakh contracts at the end of October, to about seventy thousand. When short sellers buy back, it adds fuel to a rally. What it means for you: when foreign money flows in, big banks and index heavyweights usually feel it first. If you invest through index funds, you are already riding it. No action needed.

chapters.title: Banks lead, IT lags
chapters.text: Story two. Banks led the day. The Nifty P S U Bank index jumped almost three per cent, and the Nifty Bank index rose one point eight per cent. I T, pharma and real estate stocks slipped about half a per cent. Across the Nifty one hundred, Bank of Baroda led with a jump of almost six per cent, followed by Mahindra and Mahindra, and Samvardhana Motherson. Adani Green Energy fell the most, down more than three per cent, with L T M and Adani Ports also lower. What it means for you: a rally led by banks usually reflects confidence in the economy and in loan growth. If your portfolio leans towards I T, you may have felt left out on Wednesday. That is normal. Sectors take turns.

chapters.title: Oil slips below 90 dollars
chapters.text: Story three. Oil is getting cheaper. On Tuesday, Brent crude briefly fell below ninety dollars a barrel, for the first time since August, after President Trump said the Iran war could end soon. By Wednesday afternoon it was around ninety three dollars, still about twenty five per cent below its late October peak of more than one hundred and seventeen. India imports most of its oil, so cheaper crude helps keep inflation and the import bill in check. What it means for you: if this holds, it eases pressure on fuel and cooking gas costs over time, and on companies that use crude as a raw material, like paint and tyre makers.

chapters.title: Silver and gold climb
chapters.text: Story four. Silver shone. On the M C X, silver rose almost three per cent, to about one lakh, eighty eight thousand rupees a kilo. Gold rose three quarters of a per cent, to about one lakh, forty one thousand, six hundred rupees for ten grams. What it means for you: precious metals have had a huge run. If you are buying gold or silver for a wedding or a festival, remember that prices can swing a few per cent in a single day.

chapters.title: Anthropic's giant IPO
chapters.text: Story five, from abroad. Anthropic, the company behind the AI assistant Claude, has started its roadshow for a listing on the Nasdaq. It plans to sell eight hundred and twenty five million shares at seventy to seventy eight dollars each, raising up to sixty four billion dollars, at a valuation of up to one point four trillion dollars. Pricing is expected on the eighteenth of November. What it means for you: it is a big test of how much investors will pay for A I, and the mood around it can sway Indian I T stocks too.

chapters.title: Quick hits, term of the day, sign-off
chapters.text: Quick hits. Railway stocks R V N L and RailTel rose about five per cent. J S W Steel produced nineteen per cent more crude steel in October than a year ago. And Garden Reach Shipbuilders' quarterly profit rose about twelve per cent. One caution: the India VIX, the market's fear gauge, rose to seventeen point five six, even as the market went up. Today's term is short covering. When traders who bet on a fall buy back to close those bets, that buying itself pushes prices up. That is part of what is lifting the Nifty right now. Coming up today: weekly Sensex options expire. That is your brief. The charts and the full calendar are on the Today tab. This is Springpad Today. See you tomorrow.
